claims.text: A two-step heat treatment can induce controlled nanoscale coherent precipitates in a single-phase HEA.
The induced coherent precipitates synergistically enhance strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance.
High-temperature homogenization followed by quenching maintains a supersaturated solid solution.
Controlled lower-temperature aging induces nanoscale coherent precipitates.
Moderate aging temperatures, precise aging times, and compositions prone to controlled phase separation favor coherent-precipitate formation and stability.
Excessive precipitate growth, coarsening, or brittle intermetallic formation can eliminate the proposed benefits.
Very high operating temperatures can destabilize the precipitates.
Finely dispersed coherent precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
The precipitates permit sufficient plastic deformation to preserve or improve ductility.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces help maintain toughness.
The precipitates modify local bonding in a way that can increase Young’s modulus.
The precipitates promote crack deflection or blunting and consequently improve fracture resistance.
The treatment is expected to increase tensile strength by approximately 20–30% relative to untreated HEAs.
The treatment is expected to maintain or improve ductility relative to untreated HEAs.
The treatment is expected to noticeably increase Young’s modulus relative to untreated HEAs.
The treatment is expected to produce superior fracture toughness relative to untreated HEAs.
HEAs processed without specialized precipitation engineering typically exhibit a strength–ductility trade-off.
The hypothesis is falsified if treated samples lack statistically significant combined property improvements or if the targeted coherent precipitates are not confirmed.
